ae5ed1ada1a1e815a2c94077152490ba179b4c4e.summary: A GitHub repository by an individual (cdong1012) containing a Python tool called ContiUnpacker. It uses the Speakeasy Emulation Framework to try to unpack a packed Conti ransomware sample found on MalwareBazaar. The author says the tool does not work fully: only parts of a section are written during emulation, so the dumped executable may not run. The repository page was archived on 2026-11-25. It is a tool write-up, not a vendor threat report.

tools.q: The unpacker uses the Speakeasy Emulation Framework to run and unpack the sample.

ae1c5029f534c284cbea2309da3008c1ed4fda87.summary: BleepingComputer reports an alleged Netwalker ransomware attack on data center provider Equinix over the 2020 Labor Day weekend. The ransom note demanded $4.5 million (455 bitcoin), doubling to $9 million if unpaid, and threatened to publish allegedly stolen data. Equinix said it detected ransomware on some internal systems, notified law enforcement and remained operational. Advanced Intel reported 74 Equinix RDP servers with credentials for sale, mostly in Australia, Turkey and Brazil.

ae3c675344b1fce1024af5af4390c5a11e42abcb.summary: Fortinet's December 2019 blog describes BIOLOAD, a loader that uses DLL search order hijacking through the FaceFodUninstaller.exe host process, started by a scheduled task. It carries an embedded Carbanak backdoor, decrypted with a key derived from each victim's machine name. The report attributes the loader to FIN7, based on shared code and techniques with BOOSTWRITE. Samples were compiled in 2019, and the report calls this the first public case of this host process being abused.
